# Coupling to snapy and paddle {#sec-ch14}

This chapter describes what a dynamical core calls in kintera and which conventions both sides must share. The
hydrodynamic code snapy uses kintera as its equation of state and for saturation adjustment at the end of the
last stage of each step, when the card has nucleation reactions.
Its example drivers and the Python driver paddle call the kinetics of @sec-ch06 once per step, after the
dynamics. kintera has no test of its own for these call sites. The derivations below rest on the calling code at the
pins of `tools/package-pins.json`, and the check script `check_ch14_coupling.py` rebuilds each conversion, the
saturation adjustment and the kinetics hand-back with inputs built as snapy builds them; no coupled snapy run was
made.

The dependency map of the schemes is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| scheme | YAML key or option | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| @sec-ch14-thermo | the thermodynamics card | always | exact | check `check_ch14_coupling.py` (a)-(j) |
| @sec-ch14-saturation | the thermodynamics card | when it has nucleation reactions | n/a | check `check_ch14_coupling.py` (k)-(r) |
| @sec-ch14-kinetics | `reactions`[^rg-ef7fafdef84f] | driver | first | check `check_ch14_coupling.py` (s)-(w) |
